corrections.finding: Measure dropped: 'the next season most are singing' omits the source's 112 singers (Noad 2000: most of 112), leaving 82 with no pair.
corrections.fixed_text: Humpback whales of the east Australian coast sing a song; in one season 2 of 82 singers are singing a new song nearly the same as the west Australian whales' song, the next season most of 112 singers are singing the old or the new and three a song mixing both, and in under two years the new song alone is sounding. Across six Pacific populations over a decade, songs pass almost always eastward, once westward, from the east Australian population toward French Polynesia over about two years, a new song typically becoming dominant within one breeding season; most songs blend the past year's material with new material, occasionally a completely new song, and how songs pass between populations, by a few males moving or by whales hearing songs while swimming together on migration, is only suspected.
